intro.title: Fulgurite Fusion
intro.text:
Harness the storm.

This map follows the mod from your first lightning strike to the Fusion Reactor. Topics light up as you find their items.

Power in this mod is Fulmen (Fm): make it from fuel, store it, move it, and spend it.

Drag to move, scroll to zoom. Click a topic to spread its cards, click a card to read it. Right-click goes back.

pages.title: Glass made by lightning
pages.text:
When lightning strikes sand, it fuses a vein of Raw Fulgurite down into the ground.

A lightning rod standing on a block passes its strike to the block below it, so a rod on sand grows fulgurite on demand. Stand rods on sand and wait for a thunderstorm.

pages.title: Mining it
pages.text:
Mine Raw Fulgurite for 4-8 Fulgurite Shards (Silk Touch gives the block itself).

Nine shards craft into two Fulgurite, the mod's main material.

pages.title: Fulmen (Fm)
pages.text:
Fm is the mod's power. Generators push it into machines touching them, batteries store it, and wires carry it between Machine Connectors.

Rates are in Fm per tick (Fm/t); there are 20 ticks in a second.

pages.title: Fulgurite tools
pages.text:
Fulgurite tools and the Fulgurite Sword sit between diamond and netherite: tougher and faster than diamond.

Every hit adds a little lightning damage (+1 for tools, +2 for the sword) with a crackle of sparks.

They wear out like normal tools; repair them with Fulgurite. Later, the Storm Forge upgrades them into Stormforged gear.

pages.title: Fulgurite Spear
pages.text:
Hold right-click to wind up, let go to throw it like a trident, then pick it up where it lands.

8 damage in melee, 9 thrown, each with +2 lightning. It wears out like the other Fulgurite tools; repair it with Fulgurite.

pages.title: Arc Magnet
pages.text:
Right-click to switch it on or off. While it glows, it pulls items and XP within 6 blocks to you. It needs no power.

Items you've just dropped are left alone for a moment, so you can still throw things away.

pages.title: Backpacks
pages.text:
Right-click to open, or press B to open the one you're wearing or carrying.

Wear it in your chestplate slot (or Curios' back slot, if installed) to carry it on your back.

Sneak + right-click a block to set it down; it opens like a chest and keeps everything when you break it.

pages.title: Bigger backpacks
pages.text:
Copper: 27 slots.
Iron: 54 slots. Craft a Copper Backpack with 4 Iron Sheets and 4 Silver Ingots.
Fulgurite: 81 slots. Craft an Iron Backpack with 4 Fulgurite and 4 Gold Sheets.
Stormforged: 108 slots. Storm Forge: Fulgurite Backpack + 2 Refined Fulgurite + a Strong or Jackpot fuel (250,000 Fm).

Upgrading keeps everything inside.

Prime Backpack (Storm Forge): a Stormforged Backpack + a Prime Spark Fragment + a Block of Gold + a Block of Silver, 5,000,000 Fm. 120 slots, 7 upgrade slots, a 2,000,000 Fm store, and it takes Storm upgrades.

pages.title: Upgrades
pages.text:
Upgrades go in the slots left of the storage (Copper 1, Iron 2, Fulgurite 3, Stormforged 5), one of each kind.

Pickup: picked-up items go into the pack.
Magnet (Iron+): pulls items from 6 blocks.
Void: destroys listed items you pick up.
Compacting (Fulgurite+): packs 2x2 sets into blocks.

pages.title: Upgrade filters
pages.text:
Right-click an upgrade in your hand to set its filter. Click an item into a filter slot to list it (it's only a copy); click with an empty hand to clear.

Allow list: only listed items. Block list: everything except them. Pickup, Magnet and Compacting start as an empty block list (everything). Void starts as an allow list, and an empty Void list destroys nothing.

Compacting only packs blocks that craft back into the same items.

pages.title: Storm upgrades
pages.text:
Storm Forge: basic upgrade + Refined Fulgurite + Overcharged Spark Cell (100,000 Fm). Stormforged Backpack only.

They run on the pack's own Fm (charge it in a Fulgurite Charger); without Fm they act like the basic upgrade.
Pickup: grabs items within 3 blocks (also when the pack is set down).
Magnet: 12 blocks.
Void: can also remove XP orbs.
Compacting: 3x3 as well.

pages.title: Utility upgrades
pages.text:
Feeding: eats from the pack when you're hungry (never wastes food; skips harmful food unless allow-listed).
Refill: tops up hotbar stacks.
Restock / Deposit (Iron+): buttons beside an open chest.
Tool Swapper (Fulgurite+): best tool from the pack when you start mining.

pages.title: Storm utility
pages.text:
Feeding: heals you when you're full.
Refill: instant; also offhand, and re-equips armor that breaks.
Restock / Deposit: look at a container (8 blocks), open the pack, use its buttons (500 Fm).
Tool Swapper: also swaps in your best weapon when you attack (the next hit uses it).

pages.title: Your first generator
pages.text:
Strike a vanilla furnace with lightning (a lightning rod on top works) and it becomes a Weak Storm Furnace.

It burns fuel into Fm and pushes it into machines touching any face except its front.

pages.title: Fuel
pages.text:
Every fuel is worth a fixed amount of Fm: one coal is 5,120 Fm. Other fuels scale with how long they burn in a normal furnace.

Higher tiers don't get more out of a fuel, they deliver it faster:
 Weak: 16 Fm/t
 Enhanced: 32 Fm/t
 Charged: 64 Fm/t

pages.title: Grounding
pages.text:
An ungrounded Storm Furnace builds up static and shocks players nearby. The shock gets stronger with each tier.

Ground it with three lightning rods stacked straight down under the furnace. Its menu shows whether it's grounded.

pages.title: Upgrade ritual
pages.text:
Lightning upgrades a Storm Furnace one tier if the right offerings are in place. Blocks go against all four side faces; items are dropped on top.

Weak to Enhanced: 4 copper blocks, 2 Charged Spark Cells, 4 Magnetite Ingots.

Enhanced to Charged: 4 gold blocks, 6 Charged Spark Cells, 6 Silver Ingots.

If anything is missing, nothing upgrades, and the lightning will likely burn your offering.

pages.title: Bottled power
pages.text: Empty Spark Cells hold a little Fm. They're used in recipes, the ritual and the colliders.

pages.title: Fulgurite Charger
pages.text:
Charges Empty Spark Cells: 1,280 Fm each, drawing 16 Fm/t (4 seconds a cell).

It passes power on to machines touching it, so it can sit in a daisy chain.

pages.title: Stronger cells
pages.text:
Charged and Overcharged Spark Cells are made in the Storm Collider:

Spark Cell + Redstone Block = Charged Spark Cell

Charged Spark Cell + Arc Core = Overcharged Spark Cell

pages.title: Storm Battery
pages.text:
Holds 64,000 Fm. Touching batteries form a bank (up to 6) that fills and drains as one, with one big gauge across the whole bank.

Open the menu and press I/O to set each face to In, Out, Both or None (Both by default). The setting covers the whole bank.

In: power can enter there. Out: the bank feeds touching machines and wire connectors on that face.

pages.title: Machine Connector
pages.text:
Sticks to any face of any block, like a torch.

On a machine it links that machine to a wire network. On a plain block (fence, wall, log) it's a relay, so you can build power poles. On a multiblock machine only the power port takes one.

Right-click it with an empty hand to see the network's status.

pages.title: Wires
pages.text:
Wire Rolls string hanging wires between connectors: use the roll on one connector, then the next.

Three gauges, each raw (bare copper) or insulated:
 Basic: 16 blocks, 256 Fm/t.
 Reinforced: 32 blocks, 512 Fm/t.
 Heavy: 64 blocks, 1024 Fm/t, hangs taut.

Raw wire is cheap but, while power flows, shocks anyone near it and electrifies water. Thicker raw wire bites harder: Basic 1 heart, Reinforced 2, Heavy 4 hearts and sets you alight. Insulate it in the Wire Extruder with Malleable Rubber (see Rubber).

A network carries only as much as its weakest wire. Upgrade every span to raise the limit; a connector shows how much is flowing out of the most it can carry.

pages.title: Daisy chains
pages.text:
Machines touching each other pass power along, in any mix of types. A chain stops after 8 machines.

Batteries don't pass power through chains; they feed what they touch.

pages.title: Converters
pages.text:
FE Converter: Fm in, Forge Energy out of the front (1 Fm = 4 FE).

Universal EU Converter: Fm in on any side, EU out of the front. It matches the voltage of the GregTech or Modern Industrialization cable or machine on its front.

pages.title: Multiblock machines
pages.text:
Each machine is a cube of Arc Casings with a controller on the front face, bottom row.

Small (2x2x2): Press, Arc Furnace, Wire Extruder, Banbury Mixer. The controller is at the front-left bottom.

Large (3x3x3): Kiln, Crusher. The controller is at the front-centre bottom.

pages.title: Build: small machine
pages.text:
Small machines (Press, Arc Furnace, Wire Extruder, Banbury Mixer) are a 2x2x2 cube.

The controller goes at the front-left of the bottom layer, facing you. The other 7 blocks are Arc Casings. The lowest casing tier sets the machine's speed.

Right-click the controller to check the build: missing casings are outlined for a few seconds.

pages.title: Build: large machine
pages.text:
Large machines (Kiln, Crusher) are a 3x3x3 cube.

The controller goes in the middle of the bottom front row, facing you. The other 26 blocks are Arc Casings. The lowest casing tier sets the machine's speed.

pages.title: Arc Casings
pages.text:
A machine runs at the tier of its lowest casing. Each tier runs twice as fast as the one before:
 Crude 1x, Tempered 2x, Charged 4x, Prime 8x.

pages.title: Ports
pages.text:
Once a machine is built, glowing markers show its ports.

Power port (yellow, filled square): top layer, at the back. A Machine Connector goes on it.

Input port (green, plus): top layer, at the front. A hopper above fills the machine.

Output port (orange, minus): bottom layer, at the back. A hopper below (or a pipe beside) empties it.

Right-click any part of the machine to open its menu, even with something in your hand. Sneak to place blocks against it.

pages.title: What they make
pages.text:
Press: copper, iron, gold and silver ingots into sheets, and Magnetite Ingots into Magnetite Plates; 4 Fulgurite Shards into a Fulgurite.

Wire Extruder: a Copper Sheet into 2 Raw Wire; 2 Raw Wire + an Iron Sheet into 2 Raw Reinforced Wire; raw wire + Malleable Rubber into insulated wire.

Kiln: 2 Fulgurite into a Coil Segment. Sand + a Fulgurite Shard makes 4 Fulgurite Blast Glass; Cobbled Deepslate + a shard makes 4 Reinforced Fulgurite.

Arc Furnace: anything a furnace smelts, and a Latex Bucket into 2 Dried Rubber.

Banbury Mixer: Dried Rubber into Malleable Rubber.

Crusher: a Raw Fulgurite block into 10 shards; raw ore (iron, copper, gold, Magnetite, Argentite) into 2 crushed ore (smelt it into ingots).

pages.title: The collider ring
pages.text:
A 7x7 ring, one layer, with the collider block in the middle:

 21 Fulgurite Ring blocks round the edge
 1 Collider Input in the middle of one side
 2 Collider Injectors in the middle of the two sides next to it
 the fourth side's middle is a ring block

pages.title: Build: collider ring
pages.text:
The Mini Collider sits in the middle of a 7x7 ring, all on one level.

A Collider Input goes in the middle of the side you'll load from. A Collider Injector goes in the middle of each of the two sides next to it. The other 21 spots are Fulgurite Ring blocks.

Tip: a lever on the Mini Collider shows a ghost outline of whatever is still missing.

pages.title: A shot
pages.text:
Two Spark Cells leave the input in opposite directions, run one full lap of the ring, then carry on to the first injector they reach, which fires them into the middle to collide.

In the Mini Collider each collision releases 20,480 Fm over 8 seconds. Power comes out of the top: a machine or battery on top, or a Machine Connector.

Right-click any part of the ring for its menu.

pages.title: Pairing machine
pages.text:
Swap the Storm Collider in for the Mini Collider and the ring becomes a pairing machine.

Each injector holds one material; every shot carries one from each into the middle and the pair decides the result. It costs 4,096 Fm a shot, fed from any side or a connector on top.

Products come out of the bottom into a hopper or pipe, or sneak + right-click to take them.

pages.title: Build: Storm Collider
pages.text:
The Storm Collider uses the same 7x7 ring as the Mini Collider: a Collider Input in the middle of one side, a Collider Injector in the middle of each side next to it, and Fulgurite Ring blocks everywhere else.

A lever on the Storm Collider shows the ghost outline.

pages.title: Crafting pairs
pages.text:
Fulgurite + Fulgurite = Refined Fulgurite

Prime Spark Fragment + Prime Spark Fragment = Prime Spark

Spark Cell + Redstone Block = Charged Spark Cell

Charged Spark Cell + Arc Core = Overcharged Spark Cell

pages.title: Fusion Fuel
pages.text:
Pair two exotic materials and the collision makes a Fusion Fuel capsule for the Fusion Reactor, sometimes with a byproduct.

This is the safe way to find out what a pairing does: bad results here only shock, smoke or knock back. They never break blocks.

pages.title: The twelve
pages.text:
Twelve rare materials, each with its own energy. Any two can be paired, 78 pairings in all, and each has its own result.

The next pages say where each one comes from.

pages.title: Sky Collector
pages.text:
Aurora Dust and Sunmote fall from the sky. Place a Sky Collector under open sky:

Clear nights, at Y 200 or higher: Aurora Dust (about one every 25 seconds).

Clear middays in a desert or badlands: Sunmote (about one every 15 seconds).

Hoppers can empty it, or right-click it with an empty hand. Right-click when it's empty to see what it's waiting for.

pages.title: Abyssal Nacre
pages.text:
Build an active Conduit in a deep ocean. Abyssal Nacre Clusters slowly grow on prismarine (plain, bricks or dark) touching water near it, up to 16 at a time.

Mine a cluster for 1-3 Abyssal Nacre.

pages.title: Soul Frost
pages.text:
Empty a bucket of powder snow onto soul fire. It freezes into Frozen Soul Fire.

Break it for 2-4 Soul Frost.

pages.title: Echo Resin
pages.text:
Right-click sculk with an axe in the Deep Dark to scrape off Echo Resin (most scrapes give one).

Careful: scraping is loud, and the sculk can hear it.

pages.title: Gale Core
pages.text: Breezes in Trial Chambers often drop a Gale Core.

pages.title: Stormwing Plume
pages.text: Shake one loose by hitting a Stormwing. See the Stormwings chapter.

pages.title: Null Scale
pages.text: Dropped by Voidmoths, which flutter round the outer End islands and are drawn to End Rods. Hitting one drains your experience.

pages.title: Lumen Gel
pages.text: Lumen Slugs crawl through the Lush Caves leaving a glowing trail. Scoop the trail with a glass bottle: no need to hurt the slug.

pages.title: Cinder Heart
pages.text: Large Magma Cubes in the Basalt Deltas sometimes drop a Cinder Heart.

pages.title: Wither Ash
pages.text: Wither Skeletons killed by lightning, or within a minute of being struck, drop 2-4 Wither Ash. Lure them out of the Nether into a storm, or near a lightning rod.

pages.title: Struck Spore
pages.text: When lightning strikes a Mooshroom, shear it within a minute for 2-3 Struck Spores.

pages.title: Pairing results
pages.text:
Fizzle: no reaction, wasted.
Steady: reliable power.
Strong: lots of power.
Jackpot: huge power, sometimes a rare byproduct.
Unstable: big but spiky; shocks.
Bad: poor power, smoke and harm.
Catastrophic: an explosion, and in the reactor, real damage.
Wildcard: Struck Spore pairings roll a different result each time.

pages.title: Learning them
pages.text: Pairings you've made are remembered, so you learn which are safe. Try new pairings in the Storm Collider first: there, a bad result can't wreck anything.

pages.title: Storm eagles
pages.text:
Great storm birds that nest on the high peaks: jagged, frozen and stony.

In clear or rainy weather they sit calmly on their nests. In a thunderstorm they circle and attack any player they see, and once they fight you they don't give up.

Hurt and angry, they dive with lightning.

pages.title: Plumes and guards
pages.text:
Hitting a Stormwing can shake loose a Stormwing Plume.

A bird sitting on its nest sheds Molted Plumes into the bowl now and then.

Every so often a Stormwing flies off to hunt. While it's away an Arc Serpent guards the nest.

pages.title: Storm Caller
pages.text:
Hold right-click for 2 seconds to call a thunderstorm (5 minutes). It costs a Charged Spark Cell, and only works from clear skies under open sky.

Any thunderstorm wakes the Stormwings up.

pages.title: Eggs
pages.text:
About one nest in ten holds a Stormwing Egg.

An egg only warms beside a running Storm Collider, and hatches after 20-40 minutes of it. Whatever the collider fires while the egg warms shapes the bird inside, and risky pairings can hatch something wild.

pages.title: Hatchlings
pages.text:
A hatchling can't fly yet: it walks, leaps and glides. It grows up after one Minecraft day.

A loyal hatchling follows the player who placed the egg. Right-click it with an empty hand to make it stay or follow; it keeps that when it grows up. A grown loyal bird follows you, sits on command and defends you.

A feral one runs from everyone and grows into a dangerous bird.

pages.title: Thunderbond Talisman
pages.text:
Bonds a Stormwing to you so you can ride it. Tie 4 Molted Plumes with string to make a Molted Plume Bundle first.

A wild Stormwing only bonds during a thunderstorm, and only while it's calm. Your own hatched bird bonds any time.

The talisman is used up when the bond takes.

pages.title: Riding
pages.text:
Right-click your bonded Stormwing with an empty hand to ride. Sneak + right-click to make it stay or follow.

It flies where you face: W/A/S/D to move, Space to climb, Shift to descend. Shift lets you off once you're down near the ground.

Press R for a lightning dive: it lunges and calls lightning onto what you aim at (every 5 seconds).

In a thunderstorm it fills Empty Spark Cells in your inventory as you fly.

pages.title: Storm Forge
pages.text:
The Storm Forge pours huge amounts of Fm into gear. Build it:

- the Storm Forge (anvil) on top of a 5x5 floor of Tempered Arc Casing
- a pylon on each floor corner: 2 Reinforced Fulgurite with a Lightning Rod on top

Power it with a redstone signal to see a ghost of the build.

pages.title: Build: Storm Forge
pages.text:
The Storm Forge stands on a 5x5 floor of Tempered Arc Casing, one block below it.

At each corner of the floor, a pillar of 2 Reinforced Fulgurite topped with a Lightning Rod.

Forge Power Ports can replace any floor casing on the edges (not the corners).

A lever on the forge shows the ghost outline.

pages.title: Powering the forge
pages.text:
The forge draws up to 8,192 Fm/t. Feed Fm into the anvil itself, or swap any edge casing of the floor (not a corner) for a Forge Power Port and feed that: a battery, a wire, or the back of a reactor Power Port.

Sneak + right-click the anvil with an empty hand to see its status.

pages.title: Forging
pages.text:
Right-click the anvil with an item to set one on it. When the items match a recipe, arcs jump from the pylons and the forge fills them with Fm. When it's done, right-click to take the result.

Empty hand: take the last item back (any Fm already spent on it is lost).

Forged gear keeps the enchantments and name of the item it came from, and comes out half charged.

pages.title: Stormforged armor
pages.text:
Forge: a diamond armor piece + 2 Refined Fulgurite + 1 Strong or Jackpot Fusion Fuel, for 500,000 Fm.

Netherite-level protection that never breaks. Its abilities run on stored Fm (1,000,000 per piece) and stop when a piece is empty.

Recharge in a Fulgurite Charger. Small bars left of your XP bar show each piece's charge.

pages.title: Stormforged abilities
pages.text:
Full set: lightning can't hurt you (strikes recharge every piece), knockback resistance and faster movement.

Helmet: breathe underwater. It splits water for oxygen and stores the hydrogen: 10 minutes until the tank is full. Surface and it vents on its own. Don't vent near fire or lava!

Boots: fall damage cut to a quarter.

pages.title: Stormforged tools
pages.text:
Forge a Fulgurite tool + 2 Refined Fulgurite + 1 Strong or Jackpot Fusion Fuel (500,000 Fm).

Faster than netherite, never break, run on Fm (blue bar). Sneak + right-click the air to switch mode:

Arc Smelting: drops come out smelted.
Vein Mining: breaks the whole connected vein or tree (up to 64 blocks).

pages.title: Storm weapons
pages.text:
Storm Blade (from a Fulgurite Sword): 11 damage +4 lightning; every hit chains lightning to up to 5 nearby enemies.

Storm Spear (from a Fulgurite Spear): 11 melee, 13 thrown +4 lightning, and a charged throw calls lightning down where it lands.

Both lose their lightning when out of Fm.

pages.title: Tempest Staff
pages.text:
Forge it from a Tempest Crystal, 2 Refined Fulgurite, 2 Stormquartz and a Charged Spark Cell (500,000 Fm).

Right-click to call lightning where you aim, up to 32 blocks. Each strike costs 10,000 Fm and deals 8 damage around where it lands, setting mobs on fire. It never burns blocks and never hits you or your pets.

Recharge it in a Fulgurite Charger.

pages.title: Prime gear
pages.text:
The last step: forge any Stormforged piece + a Prime Spark Fragment + a Block of Gold + a Block of Silver, for 20,000,000 Fm. Enchantments and names carry over.

Prime gear holds 8,000,000 Fm (violet bar), protects and hits harder, and keeps every Stormforged ability.

pages.title: Prime armor
pages.text:
Boots: no fall damage.

Full Prime set:
- Glide: jump in mid-air to spread out and glide like an elytra (400 Fm a second from the chestplate).
- Boost: while gliding, hold jump to rocket along the way you look.
- Static discharge: anything that hits you takes 8 lightning damage and is thrown back (2,000 Fm a time).

It also counts as a full Stormforged set.

pages.title: Prime tools and weapons
pages.text:
Prime Pickaxe: press V (rebindable) to toggle the 3x3 hammer. It breaks a 3x3 square facing you, only blocks the pickaxe can mine. Sneak + right-click still cycles Arc Smelting and Vein Mining (vein mining pauses while the hammer is on).

Prime Blade: 19 damage +12 lightning; lightning chains to 8 enemies.

Prime Spear: hits for 14, thrown for 17 +6 lightning, and flies back to you after every throw.

pages.title: Overview
pages.text:
The Fusion Reactor fires two fuels round two huge rings and smashes them together in a blast chamber, for enormous amounts of Fm.

It has four parts: the blast chamber with the Fusion Collider in its middle, the inner ring, the outer ring and the control console.

Every part is explosion-proof. Right-click the Fusion Collider to see what's missing.

pages.title: Build: Fusion Reactor
pages.text:
Everything is built around the Fusion Collider.

Blast chamber: a 5x5x5 shell around it. Blast Chamber Frame on the edges, Fulgurite Blast Glass on the faces, left open on two opposite sides.

Inner ring: a tube 9 blocks out, with Fusion Injectors facing the chamber and two Receiver Portals.

Outer ring: a tube 44 blocks out, with two Transfer Portals and the Ring Injection Ports.

It's big: put a lever on the Fusion Collider and follow the ghost outline.

pages.title: Ghost outline
pages.text:
Not sure where a block goes? Give the Fusion Collider a redstone signal (a lever on it works) and every block still missing shows as a faint glowing ghost. Red boxes mark spots that must be left empty.

Where you have a choice (which way the chamber opens, which corners hold the portals), the ghost follows what you've already placed.

The Reactor Control Console, the Storm Collider and the Mini Collider show ghosts the same way.

pages.title: Blast chamber
pages.text:
A hollow 5x5x5 cube with the Fusion Collider in the very middle.

Edges: Blast Chamber Frame. Faces: Fulgurite Blast Glass. Leave the middle block of two opposite side faces open (east and west, or north and south): that's where the beams come in.

Once it's right it forms on its own into an armoured sphere with portholes.

pages.title: The ring tubes
pages.text:
Both rings are the same diamond-shaped tube running round a square channel: glass at the four tips (top, bottom, inside, outside), Reinforced Fulgurite on the four diagonals, and air down the middle.

The inner ring's channel is 9 blocks out from the collider, the outer ring's 44 blocks out.

When everything is right the tubes form into smooth glowing rings.

pages.title: Inner ring parts
pages.text:
Two Fusion Injectors on the inner ring's inside face, 7 blocks out from the collider, in line with the chamber's open faces, fronts facing the chamber.

Two Receiver Portals on its outside face, at opposite corners, at the end of a straight side.

pages.title: Outer ring parts
pages.text:
Two Transfer Portals on the outer ring's inside face, each straight in line with a Receiver Portal. The charge jumps across the open air between them, so keep that gap clear.

Two Ring Injection Ports on the outside face at one corner, each in line with the channel of the other side. They replace the middle outer glass there.

pages.title: Control console
pages.text:
7 wide, 3 tall, 1 deep. Place the Reactor Control Console (control panel) first, facing you, in the middle of the middle row. Seen from the front:

Top: casings all along.
Middle: Power Port, casing, casing, CONTROL PANEL, casing, casing, Power Port.
Bottom: casing, Fuel Input, Data Port, casing, Data Port, Fuel Input, casing.

Once formed, the casings turn into the frame, power gauge, displays and fuel screens.

pages.title: Build: control console
pages.text:
The console is a wall 7 blocks wide and 3 tall, with the Reactor Console in the middle of the middle row.

Bottom row: Console Fuel Inputs in the 2nd and 6th spots, Console Data Ports in the 3rd and 5th.
Middle row: a Console Power Port at each end.
Everything else: Console Casing.

A lever on the console shows the ghost outline.

pages.title: Data cables
pages.text:
Run a Data Cable from each Console Data Port to a Ring Injection Port, one cable per port. The left port carries fuel 1, the right fuel 2. Keep the two cables apart, and each under 128 blocks.

The cable is a free-standing metal pipe with smooth bends.

The rings only form once both cables are connected.

pages.title: Fuel
pages.text:
Each fuel slot takes a Fusion Fuel capsule or a raw exotic material. Load them in the console's menu, or with hoppers or pipes into the Fuel Inputs from the front or back.

Two capsules: both capsules' power added, then doubled. The best.
Two raw materials: their pairing's normal power.
One of each: in between.

pages.title: A run
pages.text:
Each run needs an 8,000 Fm startup charge. The console takes it from a battery or generator behind a power port.

Press Start (or turn Auto on). The two charges fire from the Ring Injection Ports and race opposite ways round the outer ring for 6 laps, 30 seconds, speeding up all the way.

They jump from the Transfer Portals to the Receiver Portals, scream through 6 laps of the inner ring, and are fired into the chamber to collide.

pages.title: Power out
pages.text:
The collision's Fm fills the console's store (16,000,000 Fm). The power ports push it out of their backs, 4,096 Fm/t each, into a battery or machine behind them. A Machine Connector on a Power Port links the console into a wire network as a power source.

Byproducts come out at twice the Storm Collider's rate, into the console's byproduct slot. Take them in the menu, or put a hopper under a Fuel Input.

The menu shows the store, the run's progress and the last result.

pages.title: When it goes wrong
pages.text:
A cut data cable: that injector gets no fuel. The other charge fires anyway, finds nothing to hit, and is lost.

Something in a portal beam's path: that charge fizzles out.

Every pairing has its own reaction: crops ripen, water freezes, coral grows, Drowned rise, lightning storms strike, the area stays charged with static... Some fuels overheat the reactor, and it must cool down before the next run.

The worst can tear blocks out of the chamber (Chamber Breach) or melt part of the ring back into Raw Fulgurite (Ring Melt). The reactor stays down until you replace them.

Watching a fuel burn teaches you what it does. A lost run turns Auto off.

pages.title: Rubber trees
pages.text:
Tall, slim trees with pale bark that grow in jungles and swamps. Their leaves drop saplings, and wandering traders sometimes sell them.

The wood makes pale planks like any other log.

pages.title: Tapping latex
pages.text:
Put a Tree Tap on the side of a Rubber Log, then set an empty bucket on the ground under it: right-click the top of a block with the bucket. It can be up to 6 blocks below the tap.

Latex drips into the bucket. After about 4 minutes it's full: break it (or right-click it) to get a Latex Bucket.

Right-click a bucket that's still filling to see how far along it is.

pages.title: Latex Harvester
pages.text:
A 3x3x2 ring around the bottom two blocks of a Rubber Log trunk. On the top layer's front row: the controller in the middle (facing you), a Harvester Tank in one corner with a second Harvester Tank under it, and a Harvester Power Port in the other corner. The other 12 blocks are Arc Casings of one tier. Right-click the controller to see what's missing.

Probes stab into the bark through the windows: it taps 1.5 buckets a minute with Crude casings and uses 32 Fm/t. Each better tier doubles both. The tank holds 128 buckets and the harvester stops when it's full. Drain it with a bucket or a fluid pipe.

Every tree holds 1,000 to 4,000 buckets, rolled when you finish the build. When it runs out the trunk turns to Dried Rubber Logs. Chop the tree, plant a new sapling in the ring, and the harvester gives it extra growth ticks (500 Fm each).

pages.title: Build: Latex Vulcanizer
pages.text:
A small (2x2x2) machine: the controller at the front-left of the bottom layer, facing you, and 7 Arc Casings.

Pipe latex into any casing from any side except the front (a Latex Harvester's tank works), pour in a Latex Bucket by right-clicking a casing, or put Latex Buckets in its input slots. The vat holds 16 buckets.

Each bucket cures into 3 Dried Rubber on the heated drum, one more than the Arc Furnace gives. The rubber comes out of the output port like any machine.

pages.title: Fluid Pipe
pages.text:
Copper pipe with a glass window. It joins other Fluid Pipes and anything that holds fluid.

No setup: a pipe touching a tank that only gives fluid out (a Latex Harvester's tank) pulls from it, up to 1 bucket a second, and delivers along the line to anything that takes fluid in (any side of a Latex Vulcanizer but the front).

The window shows latex while it's flowing. Pipes hold nothing themselves, so breaking one loses no latex.

pages.title: Dried and kneaded
pages.text:
Arc Furnace: a Latex Bucket dries into 2 Dried Rubber, and you get the bucket back.

Banbury Mixer: Dried Rubber is kneaded into Malleable Rubber.

Wire Extruder: raw wire + Malleable Rubber makes insulated wire of the same gauge. One rubber covers 4 basic, 2 reinforced or 1 heavy wire.

pages.title: Build: Banbury Mixer
pages.text:
A small (2x2x2) machine: the controller at the front-left of the bottom layer, facing you, and 7 Arc Casings.

Two heavy rotors churn the rubber while a weight presses it down from above.

pages.title: The Stormreach
pages.text: A dimension above the clouds: a vast continent of Stormstone split by deep ravines, covered in strange storm-touched life, with winding caves and huge caverns running all the way down to bedrock.

pages.title: The Storm
pages.text:
The Stormreach has its own weather, separate from the Overworld's. Long storms of 10 to 20 minutes are broken by calm spells of 2 to 4 minutes.

During a storm, lightning strikes all around you and can hit you. Its thunder is quieter than an Overworld storm's.

Where a bolt lands on Charged Stormsand, the sand fuses into Fulgurite Glass.

pages.title: Biomes
pages.text:
Stormgrass Plains: open Arcgrass meadows full of flowers, with the odd Conductor and Sparkbush.

Conductor Forest: tall, thin Conductor trees with glowing pale-blue leaves.

Thunderoak Grove: broad, twisted Thunderoaks under a dark violet canopy.

Sparkbush Thicket: dense, glowing Sparkbushes, bright even at night.

Static Marsh: low ground with pools of water and Static Reeds.

Aurora Steppe: high, windy grassland under a shimmering sky.

Glassfields: flats of Charged Stormsand with Crystal Sprouts.

Shattered Highlands: bare Stormstone, sand patches and Crystal Sprouts.

pages.title: More biomes
pages.text:
Cloudmoss Meadow: soft, pale moss ground under a misty sky, scattered with Puffblooms and drifting spores. The calmest place in the Stormreach.

Ion Lakes: wide, shallow lakes of bright blue water with grassy islands. Ion Bulbs glow on the lake floor.

Voltcap Mushroom Fields: spongy Voltcap Mycelium covered in glowing mushrooms, from small caps to giant ones.

Rubberwood Jungle: a dense, humid jungle of rubber trees, some of them giants hung with vines.

pages.title: Plants & Trees
pages.text:
Charged Loam is the Stormreach's dirt, and Arcgrass grows over it. Arcgrass spreads to nearby Loam in the light and dies back when covered. Bone meal on it grows Arcgrass, Arc Ferns and flowers. Plants and saplings, including ones from the Overworld, grow on both.

Three trees: the Conductor (tall, glowing pale-blue leaves), the Thunderoak (broad, violet leaves) and the Sparkbush (small, brightly glowing leaves). Each gives logs, planks and saplings.

Flowers glow faintly and make dyes: Voltbloom (light blue), Stormcap (purple) and Aurora Lily (magenta). Static Reeds grow in the marsh, and Crystal Sprouts grow on Stormstone in the highlands.

pages.title: Moss, bulbs and caps
pages.text:
Cloudmoss Blocks and Cloudmoss Carpet cover the meadows. Puffblooms glow softly and make white dye.

Ion Bulbs only live underwater, on the floor of a lake or pond, and light it up.

Voltcaps glow and grow on Voltcap Mycelium anywhere, or in the dark on other ground. Bone meal on a Voltcap grows a giant one. Breaking a giant cap drops a few Voltcaps.

All of these soils count as dirt, so saplings and flowers grow on them.

pages.title: Surface life
pages.text:
Sparkhorns graze the plains, steppe and highlands in herds. Breed them with Arcgrass; they drop Sparkhorn Shanks (cook them) and Horn Shards.

Pufflings bounce around the Cloudmoss Meadow. Feed one Puffblooms to tame it; right-click a tame one to sit or stand.

Rubberback Sloths live in the Rubberwood Jungle. Use an empty bucket on one for a Latex Bucket (refills in 5 minutes). Breed with Rubber Saplings.

Voltcap Snails crawl the mushroom fields and hide in their shells when hit. Breed with Voltcaps.

Glasscrabs scuttle over the Glassfields. They pinch back if attacked. Breed with Charged Stormsand.

Static Jellies drift over meadows and lakes (touching one zaps you), Ion Eels swim the Ion Lakes (hitting one shocks the water around it), and Glimmerwings flutter through the forests.

pages.title: Deep caves
pages.text:
Winding tunnels and huge open caverns run deep beneath the land, down to the bedrock floor. The dangerous creatures live down there, never under open sky.

Arcwurm: a huge armored worm. Slow, tough, and its bite slows you. Drops Arcwurm Hide.

Crystal Stalker: a crystal-grown spider that climbs walls and leaps. Its bite slows you. Sometimes drops a Tempest Crystal.

Static Wraith: a floating shadow. Each touch drains 20,000 Fm from your charged gear. Drops Wraith Essence.

Shockroach: small, fast cave roaches that come in swarms of 4-8.

Like all monsters, these don't appear on Peaceful.

pages.title: Storm hunters
pages.text:
Stormhounds: wolves of crackling static that appear in packs of 3-5 while a storm rages, and fade away when it ends.

Voltcap Crawlers: beetles with a Voltcap on their backs. At night they sit still among the mushrooms; get close and one rushes you, swells, and bursts into a cloud of stinging spores.

Stormwings also soar over the highlands, steppe and plains, nesting on the high ground. Storms wake them, just like in the Overworld.

pages.title: Resources
pages.text:
Stormstone: the dimension's stone. It drops Cobbled Stormstone, which smelts back into Stormstone. Make Polished Stormstone and Stormstone Bricks by crafting or with a stonecutter.

Fulgurite Ore: needs an iron pickaxe and drops 2 to 4 Fulgurite Shards (more with Fortune).

Tempest Crystal Ore: rare and glowing, needs a diamond pickaxe and drops a Tempest Crystal. Tempest Crystals are only found here and are kept for end-game gear.

Charged Stormsand: glowing sand on the high ground. Smelt it, or let lightning strike it, to make Fulgurite Glass. Fulgurite Glass only drops with Silk Touch.

pages.title: Lands of the Stormreach
pages.text:
The Stormreach holds twenty lands. Every climate has a common land and a rarer, stranger one beside it.

Dig down and the stone changes with you. Near the surface each land has its own rock. Below that is Stormstone, and far down is Deep Stormstone, which is slow to mine.

pages.title: Aurora Tundra
pages.text:
A frozen land of snow and glowing Aurora Ice beyond the Aurora Steppe. The ice is slick underfoot and gives off a faint light.

Aurorite ore is common under the Tundra and turns up now and then under the Steppe. Rimestone lies beneath both.

pages.title: Tempest Peaks
pages.text:
Jagged mountains of Stormslate that climb above the clouds, capped with snow.

Stormquartz forms high up, in the peaks themselves. It also appears now and then under Cloudmoss Meadows.

pages.title: Petrified Forest
pages.text:
Stone tree trunks stand in grey gravel and loam, all that's left of a forest the lightning turned to rock.

Amber ore sits in the tuff below. You'll find a little under Thunderoak Groves and Rubberwood Jungles too.

pages.title: Magnetite Fields
pages.text:
Rolling grassland broken by outcrops and boulders of dark Magnetite Rock.

Magnetite is richest here, with some under the Shattered Highlands. It's one of the two Stormreach ores that also forms in the Overworld, deep in stone and deepslate.

pages.title: Crystal Caverns Rim
pages.text:
Pale calcite ground studded with spikes of Prismite crystal, where the light turns violet.

Prismite ore lies deep, well below the surface. A little also forms under Conductor Forests and Ion Lakes.

pages.title: Fulgurite Badlands
pages.text:
Scorched sand over Fulgurite Crust, bristling with spikes of raw fulgurite. Lightning has struck here more than anywhere else.

Fulgurite ore is plentiful below, and so is Argentite, the ore of silver. Argentite also forms in the Overworld.

pages.title: Ashen Scar
pages.text:
A burnt land of ash and Cinder Rock, torn open by deep canyons. Watch your step.

Cinderite is common in the canyon walls and turns up now and then under Sparkbush Thickets and the Static Marsh.

pages.title: Stormglass Desert
pages.text:
Bright sand dunes past the Glassfields, with towers of fulgurite glass rising from them.

Tempest Crystal ore is much more common here than anywhere else. Stormsandstone lies beneath the sand.

pages.title: Smelting the new ores
pages.text:
Raw Magnetite, Raw Argentite and Raw Aurorite smelt into ingots. Cinderite, Prismite, Stormquartz and Fossil Amber drop as they are.

Raw Magnetite and Raw Argentite also go through the Crusher for double ingots. Each one packs nine to a storage block. Most need an iron pickaxe. Prismite, Stormquartz and Aurorite need diamond.

pages.title: Three guardians
pages.text:
Three guardians stand between you and the Stormreach, one in each dimension. None of them is found by chance: you summon them.

Each always drops its key piece: the Storm Eye, the Molten Heart and the Void Shard. Together they make the Storm Sigil in the Storm Forge.

pages.title: Thunderhead
pages.text: Overworld. During a thunderstorm, use a Charged Spark Cell on a Lightning Rod with open sky above it.

pages.title: Magma Conduit
pages.text: Nether. Throw a Charged Spark Cell into lava.

pages.title: Void Arc
pages.text: The End. Use an End Crystal on a Lightning Rod.

pages.title: The equipment panel
pages.text:
Open your inventory and press Gear (top right) to open the equipment panel. It has one slot for each trinket and a Back slot. Every trinket can be worn at once, and their effects stack.

The Back slot holds a backpack, so you can wear one and a chestplate at the same time. The B key still opens it.

Trinkets and the Back slot drop when you die, like the rest of your inventory. With Curios installed, trinkets go in Curios slots instead and the Gear button is hidden.

pages.title: Guardian trinkets
pages.text:
Each Storm Guardian has a 1 in 4 chance to drop its trinket.

Cloudstep Charm (Thunderhead): jump once more in mid-air, fall slower and take less fall damage. With a full Prime set, a mid-air jump opens your glide instead.

Conduit Heart (Magma Conduit): immune to fire and lava. After a lightning hit you regenerate for a few seconds.

Void Arc Band (Void Arc): press Void Blink (G) to blink 6 blocks the way you're moving. 5 second cooldown.

pages.title: Crafted trinkets
pages.text:
Grounding Charm (copper sheets, a Lightning Rod and string): lightning deals 40% less damage and can't set you on fire.

Cinder Ward (gold sheets, magma cream and a Fulgurite Shard): immune to fire. Touching lava gives you 3 seconds of lava immunity.

Seer's Ring (gold sheets, an Eye of Ender and a Fulgurite Shard): invisible and teleporting monsters within 16 blocks glow, and you're immune to Blindness and Darkness.

pages.title: Empowered trinkets
pages.text:
Forge a trinket with 4 Refined Fulgurite and one more piece in the Storm Forge (2,000,000 Fm) to empower it. A guardian trinket needs that guardian's key piece; a crafted trinket needs a Charged Spark Cell.

- Cloudstep: two extra jumps, much slower falls
- Conduit Heart: lightning heals you instead of hurting
- Void Arc Band: 10 blocks, 2.5 second cooldown
- Grounding Charm: lightning deals 70% less
- Cinder Ward: 8 seconds of lava immunity
- Seer's Ring: 32 blocks, and every monster within 12 glows

pages.title: The Storm Sigil
pages.text:
Forge the Storm Eye, Molten Heart and Void Shard with a Charged Spark Cell in the Storm Forge (5,000,000 Fm) to make a Storm Sigil.

Use it and lightning carries you into the Titan Trials, along with anyone standing within 8 blocks of you. Use it again there to come home.

pages.title: The Titan Trials
pages.text:
The Trials are a dark void with an arena of your own floating in it: a round floor ringed by eight pillars, with the Titan Altar at its heart.

Use the Storm Sigil on the altar to wake the Titan. The sigil is used up, but the Titan drops a new one each time it falls.

If you die in the Trials you wake at your bed or spawn point with everything you carried.

Words are cut into the altar's base, half worn away: "The storm-callers drew its power down through copper."

pages.title: Fighting together
pages.text:
Bring friends by standing close when you use the sigil. The Titan grows stronger for every challenger: more health, more of everything it calls, and faster attacks.

Everyone in the arena when it falls shares in the victory.

pages.title: Choosing your reward
pages.text:
Each time the Titan falls it drops one piece of Titan armor, chosen at random.

Before waking it you can offer an armor piece of Stormforged quality or better on the altar. The offering is used up, but the Titan then has a 90% chance to drop the Titan piece of that same type.

pages.title: Titan armor
pages.text:
Titan armor counts as Prime armor, so a full set keeps every Prime ability. Each piece adds 2.5 hearts.

A full Titan set also gives you:
- Regeneration while it's storming (always, in the Stormreach)
- A lightning aura that strikes monsters near you
- No knockback, and immunity to fire and lava
- Static dash: double-tap a movement key to dash that way, hurting monsters in your path (3 second cooldown)

pages.title: The Stormreach Rift
pages.text:
When the Titan falls, everyone who fought it gets a Rift Core, and the storm will know them from then on.

Craft Rift Frame blocks, and a Rift Keystone from the Rift Core. Build an upright frame like a Nether portal (inside at least 2 wide and 3 tall) with the keystone in its top edge and a Lightning Rod on the keystone. When lightning strikes the rod, the rift opens.

Only those who have defeated the Titan can pass through. Your first crossing raises a matching rift in the Stormreach to bring you home.

pages.title: The Titan Forge
pages.text:
Titan armor keeps you alive in the Stormreach. Titan Prime armor goes further: a Prime piece and the Titan piece of the same type, fused together with Stormreach ores.

The fusing happens in the Titan Forge. Craft its anvil from a Storm Forge with Blocks of Aurorite, Stormquartz, Prismite and Cinderite.

pages.title: Building it
pages.text:
Under the anvil: a 7 x 7 floor. The middle 3 x 3 is Charged Arc Casing, the rest Stormstone Bricks. Forge Power Ports can stand in for outer-edge bricks (not the corners).

On each floor corner, a Storm Pylon: 2 Stormstone Bricks, a Prismite Block, and a Lightning Rod on top.

Power the anvil with a redstone signal to see a ghost of anything still missing. Sneak and right-click it with an empty hand for its status.

pages.title: Fusing
pages.text:
Set the Prime piece, the matching Titan piece and the ores on the anvil, then feed it 50,000,000 Fm (it draws up to 32,768 Fm/t).

Helmet: 5 Aurorite Ingots, 3 Prismite Shards, 2 Fossil Amber.
Chestplate: 8 Aurorite Ingots, 4 Cinderite, 4 Stormquartz.
Leggings: 7 Aurorite Ingots, 4 Prismite Shards, 3 Cinderite.
Boots: 4 Aurorite Ingots, 3 Fossil Amber, 3 Stormquartz.

The result keeps the Prime piece's name and the best enchantments of both.

pages.title: Titan Prime armor
pages.text:
It counts as Titan armor, so every Titan, Prime and Stormforged bonus still works.

More protection and toughness than Titan, 4 hearts per piece, and 32,000,000 Fm of charge. Recharge it in a Fulgurite Charger.

pages.title: The storm bites
pages.text:
The Stormreach is home to beasts far tougher than anything in the Overworld.

Their hits are storm damage, which goes straight through normal armor. Each piece of Titan armor grounds some of it, and a full charged Titan set grounds most of it.

They also carry a static field: stand near one without a full Titan set and you take a little damage every second, feel weak, and your gear loses charge.

pages.title: When the storm rages
pages.text:
They hunt day and night, but far more of them come out during a storm.

A beast born in a storm is Storm-charged: half again as much health and harder hits.

Lightning heals them instead of hurting them.

pages.title: Roamers
pages.text:
Arc Reaver: a fast blade-armed stalker that dashes at you from a distance.

Thunderhulk: a huge, slow golem. Get close and it slams the ground, throwing you into the air.

Stormcaller Shade: floats out of reach and marks the ground under you. Move before the lightning falls.

Static Leech: leaps onto your chest and drinks your health and charge. Look down and hit it off.

pages.title: More roamers
pages.text:
Ion Swarm: a cloud of sparks that hurts everything around it. Arrows only half hurt it.

Voltspitter: keeps its distance and lobs bursting Charged Orbs.

Tempest Raptor: circles high above you, then dives.

Gloomarc Spider: climbs walls and spits slowing strands of static web.

pages.title: Signature beasts
pages.text:
Four rare elites, each found in only one biome, with a boss bar when you're near. Only one of each roams any area.

Peak Colossus (Tempest Peaks): a walking mountain. It quakes the ground, hurls charged boulders and calls lightning in a storm.

Cinder Behemoth (Ashen Scar): breathes burning ash, charges, and makes the ground erupt beneath you.

pages.title: More signature beasts
pages.text:
Aurora Wraith (Aurora Tundra): a floating spirit with a slowing beam of cold light. It calls Ion Swarms and blinks away when hurt.

Prism Sentinel (Crystal Caverns Rim): fires prism lances and shard volleys, and can refract, shrugging off most damage and turning arrows away for a few seconds.

pages.title: Spoils
pages.text:
Every beast drops its own part. These will be used to craft the gear you'll need for the Stormreach's dungeons.

A signature beast always drops its unique part, a large pile of its biome's ore, Tempest Crystals and Fulgurite Shards.

pages.title: Signature parts
pages.text: Colossus Heart, Behemoth Ember, Aurora Shroud and Sentinel Lens: the rarest parts in the Stormreach.

pages.title: Four strongholds
pages.text:
Four great dungeons are hidden in the Stormreach, each in one biome, each with more than thirty rooms, and no two alike.

Stormspire: a tower on the Tempest Peaks, built around a hollow core of lightning. Its balconies hang open over the drop, and some floors have fallen in.
Ashen Foundry: a ruined forge under the Ashen Scar, its halls flooded with lava and crossed by narrow walkways.
Aurora Sanctum: a frozen cathedral on the Aurora Tundra, with vaulted halls below.
Prism Vault: natural crystal caverns under the Crystal Caverns Rim, split by chasms.

pages.title: Inside
pages.text:
Follow the light. Only the true path to the guardian is lit, with sconces beside its doorways and lanterns along the way. Dark side passages lead to loot vaults, and to danger.

Storm Cages burst open when you come near. Arc Traps jolt you when you step on them. Tesla Coils zap anyone they can see; break them to shut them down.

pages.title: Each has its own danger
pages.text:
Storm Conductors (Stormspire) mark the ground under you; move before the lightning falls.
Crushers (Ashen Foundry) slam down onto the walkways; dust falls just before they do.
Rime Totems (Aurora Sanctum) freeze anyone who lingers near them.
Hanging Prisms (Prism Vault) break loose when you walk underneath.

All of them can be broken.

pages.title: The guardian
pages.text:
Deep inside lies the guardian's arena. Step near its altar and the dungeon's signature beast wakes, stronger than any found in the wild.

Beside the arena is the treasure vault, walled with Warded Brick and closed by a Storm Seal. Nothing breaks them until the guardian falls.

Each dungeon can be cleared only once.

pages.title: Spoils
pages.text:
Each dungeon holds its own material, found nowhere else: Skyforged Plate, Foundry Heartstone, Aurora Essence and Prism Core. They will be used for the strongest gear.

The chests also hold ore, gold, mob parts and enchanted books.

pages.title: Relics
pages.text:
Rarely, a dungeon gives up a Relic: a third, stronger tier of a trinket that's worn in the same slot.

Skyrender Charm: three extra jumps, no fall damage.
Foundry Heart: swim in lava freely.
Aurora Loop: a 14-block blink.
Prism Eye: every monster within 48 blocks glows; immune to Slowness.

They're most often found in a treasure vault.

pages.title: Storm brews
pages.text:
Stormreach parts brew like nether wart ingredients: put an Awkward Potion in a brewing stand and add the part. Gunpowder and dragon's breath make splash and lingering versions as usual.

Ion Mote: Ion Tonic. Storm damage is cut by a quarter for 3 minutes.
Volt Gland: Volt Draught. Puts 250,000 Fm into the charged gear you wear and hold.
Thunderhulk Core: Hulk's Brew. Resistance II and no knockback for 90 seconds.
Shade Veil: Veil Draught. Invisibility for 3 minutes, and storm beasts lose track of you.

pages.title: More brews
pages.text:
Leech Fang: Leech Tonic. Regeneration II for 30 seconds.
Tempest Feather: Skystep Draught. Slow Falling and Jump Boost II for 3 minutes.
Foundry Heartstone: Ember Elixir. Fire Resistance for 10 minutes.
Aurora Essence: Rime Draught. You can't freeze, and storm damage is cut by a quarter, for 8 minutes.
Prism Core: Prism Sight. Night Vision, and every monster within 32 blocks glows, for 5 minutes.

pages.title: Gadgets
pages.text:
Ion Lamp: the brightest light there is, crackling with sparks.
Storm Ward: put a Machine Connector on it and feed it Fm. While powered (20 Fm a tick) no storm beast or elite spawns within 32 blocks. Unpowered, it does nothing.
Updraft Vent: step on it to be thrown about 12 blocks up, then drift down. Sneak to stand on it safely.
Silk Rope: hang it from a ceiling, then use more rope on it to lower the line. Climbs twice as fast as a ladder.
Reaver Spikes: a floor trap that slows and cuts mobs. Players and tamed pets cross it safely.

pages.title: A farm that hunts for you
pages.text:
The Shock Farm draws mobs up out of Galvanic Soil, electrocutes them with Tesla Prongs, and gathers what they drop, and their XP, into a Farm Collector.

It spawns what the biome it stands in would spawn: monsters and animals, every vanilla mob except bosses and rare ones, and the creatures of this world from Fulgurite Fusion. Build it in a desert for husks, a swamp for slimes, the Nether for its own crowd. Light doesn't matter.

pages.title: Building it: 5x5
pages.text:
All on one floor level:
- a 3x3 pad of Galvanic Soil in the middle, with open air above it,
- a ring of Tempered Arc Casing around it,
- each corner of the ring is a pillar of 2 Reinforced Fulgurite with a Tesla Prong on top,
- the Shock Farm Controller in the middle of one edge, placed while you look toward the pad,
- at least one edge casing swapped for a Farm Collector, and one for a Farm Power Port,
- a glass wall 2 blocks high on top of every edge block, between the pillars, so nothing walks off. Any glass works.

Put a lever on the controller and switch it on: every block still missing shows as a glowing ghost, and anything in the way over the pad gets a red box. Right-click the controller to open its menu; until the farm is complete it says what's missing.

Once everything is in place the farm forms: the blocks merge into one machine with Tesla coils on its towers.

pages.title: Build: Shock Farm 5x5
pages.text: Step through it layer by layer. The controller faces the pad; the Farm Collector and Farm Power Port can take any edge spot.

pages.title: Upgrading: 7x7
pages.text:
Rebuild it bigger: a 5x5 pad of Galvanic Soil, a ring of Charged Arc Casing, and corner pillars of 3 Reinforced Fulgurite under each Tesla Prong, with the same 2-high glass wall all round. The controller still sits in the middle of an edge.

The big farm spawns twice as often, two mobs at a time, and holds up to 10 at once (the small one holds 4).

The ghost switches to the 7x7 layout as soon as you lay Charged Arc Casing on the big ring, or Galvanic Soil past the small pad.

pages.title: Build: Shock Farm 7x7
pages.text: Same layout, one ring bigger: Charged Arc Casing, a 5x5 pad and taller corner pillars.

pages.title: Running it
pages.text:
Power goes in through a Farm Power Port: put a Storm Battery against it, or run a wire or a Machine Connector to it. Each mob drawn up costs 2,000 Fm and each zap costs 100 Fm. With no power, nothing spawns and nothing is zapped.

The controller's menu shows its power, what it's doing, how many mobs are on the pad, and which mobs this biome will give you. The On/Off button stops it spawning and zapping without breaking anything; drops still get gathered.

Right-click a Farm Collector to open it. Sneak + right-click to take the stored XP. Hoppers and pipes can empty it. When every collector is full, drops pile up on the pad.

pages.title: Upgrade cards
pages.text:
The controller's menu has upgrade slots: 2 on a 5x5 farm, 4 on a 7x7. Every card in an open slot counts, and the same kind adds up.

- Mob Filter Card: right-click a mob with it to set it. The farm then only spawns the filtered mobs, and only if this biome spawns them. Sneak and use it to clear it.
- Speed Card: +50% spawn rate per tier, but each spawn costs 25% more Fm per tier.
- Efficiency Card: 15% less Fm per spawn and zap per tier, up to 75% off.
- Looting Card: +1 Looting per tier on kills (up to Looting III) and 25% more XP per tier.

Craft blank Farm Upgrade Cards first, then work each card up from Tier I to III.

pages.title: Item Pipes
pages.text:
Item Pipes join each other and any chest, barrel or machine beside them, and run as far as you like.

Right-click a pipe where it meets an inventory to switch that side between Insert (blue ring: items go in), Extract (gold collar: items are pulled out) and Off. Every Extract side shares its items out among all the Insert sides along the line.

Copper pipes move 2 items a tick, Fulgurite 16 and Stormforged 32. The pipe doing the extracting sets the speed. Watch the items slide past the glass.

pages.title: Pipe filters
pages.text:
Fulgurite and Stormforged pipes can filter. Sneak + right-click an Insert or Extract side to set up to 9 items and choose an allow list (only those) or a block list (everything but those).

On an Extract side the filter chooses what gets pulled out; on an Insert side, what that inventory will take. Copper pipes have no filters.

pages.title: Arc Transfer
pages.text:
For when a pipe is too slow: place an Arc Sender against a chest and an Arc Receiver against another, no more than 5 blocks apart. Use an Arc Tuner on the Sender, then on the Receiver, to link them.

Once a second the Sender throws its whole chest (up to 27 stacks) across in a single bolt of lightning, for 400 Fm a bolt. Power it like any machine. Sneak + use the Tuner on a Sender to unlink it.
